skill_title: Critique claims and analyse fairness / risk
notes: 20-item bank. CAPS mix: 10 L3 / 10 L4. Expected payoff = P × payoff. Fair game = expected return ≥ 0. Insurance risk-band pricing.

stimulus.inline: Coin-toss game: win R10 if heads, lose R8 if tails.
Is this game fair to player?
Roulette: bet R10 on red, win R10 with P = 18/38 (American), lose R10 with P = 20/38.
House edge per R10 bet = −R0,53 per spin.
Critique: lottery claim 'you have a 1 in 50 000 000 chance of winning'. P?
Insurance company collects R200/month from 1 000 customers (R200 000). Expected claims R150 000.
Risk band: drivers under 25 pay R350/month, over 25 pay R200. Why?

items.question: Reason?
options: Younger drivers statistically have more claims (higher P)
items.expectedAnswer: Younger drivers statistically have more claims (higher P)
workingSteps: Higher P → higher premium to cover expected payouts.

stimulus.inline: Game: roll die. Win R6 if you roll 6, lose R1 otherwise. Fair?
Game above. Verdict?
Game: lottery R5 ticket. Win R1 000 with P = 1/500.
Critique claim: 'I haven't won — so my chance of winning next is higher.'

items.question: Verdict?
options: Wrong — Independent events: past doesn't change future P (gambler's fallacy)
items.expectedAnswer: Wrong — Independent events: past doesn't change future P (gambler's fallacy)
workingSteps: Past results don't change independent future probability.

stimulus.inline: Insurance: 5% of cars claim each year, avg claim R20 000. Premium R150/month covers it?
Premium R150 × 12 = R1 800/year per car.

items.question: Does R1 800 cover expected R1 000 + overheads?
workingSteps: R1 800 income − R1 000 claim = R800 for overhead + profit.

stimulus.inline: Suburb A has 8% claim rate, suburb B 2%. Avg claim R20 000 each. Calculate expected annual claim per car in each suburb.

items.question: Suburb A vs B expected claim?

stimulus.inline: Higher risk suburb gets higher premium. Suburb A premium R2 500/yr, B R800/yr. Reasonable?

items.question: Verdict?
options: Yes — reflects expected claims plus margin
items.expectedAnswer: Yes — reflects expected claims plus margin
workingSteps: Both cover expected claim with margin.

stimulus.inline: Lottery: 1 in 250 million. Buying 10 tickets:
Carnival game: R20 to play, win R100 with P=0,1, win R5 with P=0,3, else nothing.
Net expected per game = R11,50 − R20 cost = −R8,50.

items.question: Player or house favourable?
workingSteps: Expected loss for player → house wins.

stimulus.inline: Critique claim: 'I'll keep playing until I win — eventually I must.'

items.question: Verdict?
options: Wrong — house edge means expected long-run loss is unbounded
items.expectedAnswer: Wrong — house edge means expected long-run loss is unbounded
workingSteps: Negative expected value → over time you lose more on average.

stimulus.inline: Long-term claim. Insurance company has 10 000 cars, avg annual claim per car R1 200, premium R1 800/year/car.

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_FAIR_GAME: Misjudges whether E[X] is favourable to player/house.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_RISK_BAND: Doesn't connect P to premium pricing.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_GAMBLERS_FALLACY: Believes past results affect independent future P.
